correctness.rationale: The quadratic trace identity 2Q_n=(1+√2)^n+(1−√2)^n gives Frobenius Q_{ℓm}≡Q_m mod ℓ for odd ℓ. If ℓ divides Q_m, binomial expansion with units and ℓ-adic valuations yields exact lifting v_ℓ(Q_{ℓm})=v_ℓ(Q_m)+1. The smaller odd prime p cannot divide Q_{q^b}: u=α/β in F_{p²} has order dividing p−1 or p+1, hence <q, whereas u^{q^b}=−1 would force u=−1, contradicting α+β=2 mod p; p=2 is excluded by odd parity. Thus only q can divide index gcd, and lifts to full q^b or is absent. Q4=17 and doubling imply G(3*2^a)=1 for a≥2 though entry point 2 divides the index. An independent ordinary exact recurrence/gcd scan confirmed the formula on 1,000+ two-prime-support indices through 1999; universal claim rests on Frobenius/order/lifting proof.

originality.rationale: Mbirika–Schrader–Spilker (JIS 2023) Section 6.2 Question31 explicitly seeks an index gcd formula and Conjecture32 posits an incorrect rank criterion. Their Theorem28 leaves the gcd unevaluated. The exact two-prime-support dichotomy and infinite counterfamily are not theorems there. Fiebig–Mbirika–Spilker give Lucas period/entry-point results, not the index gcd by support. Classical Lucas identities are ingredients; no identified stronger formula forces the exact all-or-nothing q^b phenomenon without additional argument.
